title: HTTP/3 WebSocket TCP Forwarder Buffering Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 WebSocket loopback test with a local TCP response server, adjacent RFC 9220 regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted RFC 9220 WebSocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler forwards two client binary WebSocket messages to a local TCP server and returns a larger TCP response as unmasked binary WebSocket messages bounded by a configured five-byte TCP forwarder buffer.
preconditions: The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
Basic TCP stream forwarding remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0011`.
expected_result: The focused TCP forwarder chunking and adjacent WebSocket regression tests pass, the new RFC 9220 TCP buffering requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 WebSocket TCP forwarder now has locally verified bounded TCP response chunk forwarding through a configured buffer. Evidence class is local same-process HTTP/3 QUIC loopback plus local loopback TCP; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
